item.title: Re: Long term use of proton pump inhibitors and risk of stomach cancer: population based case-control study in five Nordic countries
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor The study by Duru and colleagues provides a robust evaluation of the long-term relationship between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use and gastric adenocarcinoma risk (1). item.title: Re: Ultrasound should be the first line investigation for Osgood-Schlatter's disease with use of x-ray outdated.
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor X-ray is an outdated and unnecessary investigation for Osgood Schlatter’s or other growth related, traction apophyseal complaints such as Sever’s or Sinding-Larsen-Johansson. In the context of a normal, exercise related history for traction apophysitis, musculoskeletal ultrasound should be considered the first line investigation around the knee or ankle (1,2). item.title: England left behind on effective alcohol policy
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor As reported in The BMJ, Wales will increase its minimum unit pricing (MUP) of alcohol from £0.50 per unit to £0.65 from October.[1] This follows the same evidence-based step that Scotland has taken in increasing its MUP to ensure the policy’s effectiveness is not eroded by inflation. item.title: Re: Medical schools: What’s happening with the planned expansion of places in England?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Alison's piece is revealing and should be more widely made known, in my view. item.title: Better access to new medicines must not mean worse access to care for most patients
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Wise’s report (1) on the UK–US pharmaceutical agreement and Majeed’s subsequent warning (2) about implementation capture a familiar dilemma for publicly funded systems: expanding access to high-cost innovation while preserving the population health generated by everyday services. item.title: Nuclear diplomacy continues to be structurally flawed because it excludes physicians
